stored_lesson.name: membrina
complete_ordered_content: Introduce the name membrina for the color used on painted faces and nude bodies.
Take dry unground cerosa, explicitly described as white made from lead; put in a copper or iron vessel on burning coals.
Heat until it becomes yellow; then grind it.
Add white cerosa and cenobrium until flesh-like.
Leave mixture proportions to the maker and state three complexion alternatives: more cenobrium for red, more white for white, little prasinum instead of cenobrium for pale.
complete_qualifications: cerosa initially dry and not ground
mixture of colors at the maker's discretion
pale faces: a little prasinum in place of cenobrium
materials: cerosa: explicitly white material made from lead
carriers: painted faces and nude bodies; no general binder or vehicle is stated
stored_lesson.important_parameter: The source leaves mixture ratios discretionary and gives red/white/pale complexion alternatives. I.4/I.5 do not choose a unique complexion variant or exact quantity. Those remain unspecified, not secretly optimized per application.
stored_lesson.knowledge_not_physical_rerun: Stored content is the definition/preparation knowledge. Reusing the named simple preparation does NOT prove that heating/grinding is physically rerun at each mention, that a fresh batch is made, or that one old batch persists.

ordered_application_content: Mix a little cenobrium and a little minium with simple membrina.
Use it to redden the full listed set of body-image loci, retaining the written side and extent qualifications.

separating_counterconstruction.wrong_rule: Inherit the latest newly named preparation instead of the explicitly named simple base.
separating_counterconstruction.I.4_wrong_input: posc from I.3, which already carries its additional prasinum/red/little cenobrium, instead of simple membrina.
separating_counterconstruction.I.5_wrong_input: rosa from I.4, which already carries added cenobrium/minium, instead of simple membrina.
separating_counterconstruction.why_different: The source writes cum simplici membrina in both applications. A chain of latest-mixture inheritance transmits extra ingredients and a different lineage; it cannot be equated by naming the final color plausibly. This contrast is already known in IDEA390; the artifact uses it to specify information allocation rather than claiming a new discovery.

I.2: Describe prasinus as a preparation resembling green and black.
State that it is not ground on stone; put it into water, dissolve it and carefully strain through cloth.
State its usefulness as green on a fresh wall.
I.3: Presuppose that membrina has been mixed and used to fill faces and nude bodies.
Add prasinum, red burned from ochre and a little cenobrium to it.
Use that preparation to delineate every application locus enumerated below.
I.6: Mix black with a little white; call the color veneda.
Fill the depicted pupils with it.
Add more white to that color and fill the eyes on both sides.
Draw plain white between the pupil and that color.
I.7: Take posc, with the explicit phrase de quo supra dictum est.
Add more prasinum and rubeum, so that it is a shadow of the previous color.
Fill each of the listed regions.
I.8: Draw with it in the middle of the mouth so that the earlier color remains visible above and below.
Make fine strokes over rosa on the face, neck and forehead.
Use it to delineate the joints in the palms, the joints of all limbs and ungula.
I.9: State a conditional branch: if the face is dark so that one lumina does not suffice.
Draw fine strokes over the previous highlight throughout.
